dimensions.assessment: Applies nationally to federal criminal prosecutions involving homicide where a time gap occurs between the injurious act and death.
dimensions.evidence: A prosecution may be instituted for any homicide offense under this title without regard to the time that elapsed

dimensions.assessment: Allows federal murder prosecutions regardless of elapsed time, though sentencing options are capped if death occurs more than a year and a day later.
dimensions.evidence: unless the death of the victim occurred more than 1 year and 1 day after the act or omission... imprisonment for any term of years or for life

dimensions.assessment: No fiscal or economic impacts are stated or implied.
Amends chapter 51 of title 18, United States Code, by adding a section regarding federal homicide prosecution timeframes.
dimensions.evidence: Chapter 51 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change applicable to qualifying acts or omissions occurring after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: shall apply with respect to an act or omission described in that section that occurs after the date of enactment of this Act

missing_information: Estimated number of potential cases affected annually.
importance_detail.rationale: Removes federal time limits between an act or omission and a victim's death for prosecuting federal homicide offenses, while restricting the death penalty if more than a year and a day elapse.
